side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Owners active within the window, after the ratchet; every member recomputes it, else census_expected_active_mismatch.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 `active_count` (owners active in at least one of the last four periods)
note: Is active_count the raw count of owners whose recent bit is set, or the ratcheted base? CC 6.1.9 and CC 3.1.3 make it the raw count ("that count under a ratchet" is the base, computed after); CC 2.6.1.7 and its floor_applied row make it the value after the ratchet. A member recomputing one refuses the other as census_expected_active_mismatch. C156 names this as its part b; the wording of CC 2.6.1.7 is still there.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 The bit is set when the owner was active in this period or any of the previous three. It is not something recoverable from a sum.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json reads=census:member:partial&last(4); over=active/owner; combine=count(owner)
note: The text has the owner compute its own four-period bit and every member recompute the count "from the two partials" of the period. The fold cell (and the CC 8.10 card) reads the last four periods of partials and counts owners, which a sum cannot give and which counts an owner once per period it reported. The window is in the bit, not in the fold. The census model README says the same as the text.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 It is released by the first period whose count is at least two thirds of the count before the fall
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json test=count*3>=prev*2 ?open:frozen
note: The text freezes on a fall against the count before it (prev) and releases against the count before the fall (ref), a fixed reference. The fold cell has one test against prev. Read period by period, a base frozen by a fall from 30 to 10 is released the next period at 10 (10*3 >= 10*2), where the text holds it until a period returns 20. The same cell list also uses prev for the previous base in the ratchet term.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 `max_source_multiplicity` is `1` on every census composite by construction
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 The largest multiplicity cluster; aggregation_meta_multiplicity above the floor.
note: CC 6.1.9 goes on: "the census door refuses any other value". CC 2.6.1.7 and the refusal list of CC 3.1.3 apply only the R9 gate (multiplicity times n_min at most source_count), so a composite carrying 2 over a large source_count is admitted under one reading and refused under the other. No refusal token is named for the CC 6.1.9 rule.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Distinct owners behind the composite; below 10 the cell is refused census_composite_below_k.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 refusals `ballot_tally_partials_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_mass_total_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_duplicate_period`, `aggregation_meta_dominated`
note: Does the floor of ten apply to a community's secret poll? The source_count row of CC 2.6.1.7 is REQUIRED on census:composite and ballot:tally and states the refusal for both. The ballot:tally row of CC 3.1.3 lists no below-k refusal and CC 6.1.9 gives a tally only the dominance gate. A room of six that holds a poll gets a result under one reading and a refused tally under the other. The census model closes its tally instances at K = 2.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A silent member is not in the denominator. The tally is taken over **who shows up**
side_b: CC 4.5.13 The base is the standing roster at or below the count minimum the governance policy table pins and, above it, the expected-active count
note: The fallback vote on a moderation action is counted over the members who voted on that proposal in one paragraph, and over the census base in another. The policy row moderation_action has base active and floor 1/2, and CC 6.1 calls the base "a denominator a community's rules read". With 3 of 40 expected-active members voting, 2 keep-votes carry under the first and fail under the second. The census model names the first reading (ThresholdBase = responders) as the one its invariant refuses.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 The expected-active count is the community's own member-only census composite
side_b: data manifests/governance_policy.json base(N) = N if N <= k else max(min, k + (N - k) // tail); rows with base=standing use N
note: The data's base law computes the base from the roster size alone (k 12, tail 30, min 3: a roster of 100 gives 14) and its decider reads that. The text takes the base above the count minimum from the census, under the ratchet of CC 6.1.9. The data marks its law provisional and the text says "the law's constants are provisional until measured", but the two are different functions, and an implementation that replays the decider as CC 4.5.13 tells it to never reads census:expected_active.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 The floor is the standing roster at or below the count minimum of the
side_b: data manifests/governance_policy.json "min_count": {
note: The count minimum the governance policy table pins has two candidates in the data: min_count (community 2, self 1), which the decider uses as the fewest voices, and base_law.k (12), the roster size up to which the base is the roster. A reader who takes the named one gives rooms of 3 to 12 the census base; the base law gives them the roster. The census model README calls it "the small-community size".

side_a: CC 6.1.9 Counts of the mesh — nodes, links, rows held — count nodes, at most eight per owner.
side_b: CC 6.1.9 one return per owner is one source
note: C154 was read as no conflict on the ground that the return token is one per owner per period. CC 2.6.1.7 derives it from the node: "H(node_secret ‖ period)". With per-node tokens the duplicate-token refusal admits up to eight returns per owner, mass_total is then the number of returns, and the checks "mass_total = source_count" and source_count as "Distinct owners behind the composite" cannot both hold. Whether a second node of one owner is counted or dropped is not decided by the text.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3 per-node composites publish the median bucket, which moves at most one bucket below a fifth of returns forged
side_b: CC 6.1.9 A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it
note: Part 1 has the composite publish a median; CC 6.1.9 has it publish the whole histogram with exact field sums and leaves the median to the reader (the family fold says by=reader). CC 6.1.9 governs.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 Merkle root over the accepted tokens; a contributor checks its token's path against it
side_b: CC 6.1.9 A contributor recomputes `member_commitment` over the published member list and compares.
note: One check needs an inclusion path served to the contributor, the other a published list of every accepted token. CC 1.13.3.3 follows CC 6.1.9 ("over the published list"). No row is named that carries the list.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.8 a statement whose content is low-entropy, a ballot or a census cell, carries a random salt as a payload member
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "member": "salt", "type": "bstr .size 16", "presence": "required", "in_cddl": true, "cc_ref": "CC 2.6.1.8"
note: The family model requires salt today on census:share, census:member:share and ballot:tally, and not on census:composite, the partials or census:expected_active. The text states the salt only for the planned form of CC 2.6.1.8, and the signed-object table of CC 2.6.1.7 has no salt row. A share is uniformly random already; the low-entropy rows are the composite, the tally and the expected-active count.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 `census_composite_duplicate_period` (a second composite for the class and period, from any seat)
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "verbs": {"value": ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"], "source": "cc-table"
note: The family row and its CC 8.10 card give a composite (and a partial, and census:expected_active) a supersede by its author. The text refuses any second composite for a class and period, and the fold of the same family says pick=once. A reader of the text resolves it for the refusal.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 the floor is the larger of the roster's rooted-active members and half of the last stable count
side_b: data formal/census_ballot/README.md `max(owners active this period, ⌈½ · last stable composite⌉)`
note: Rooted-active members is used once and not defined. The model reads it as owners active in this period; it could be read as the expected-active (four-period) members who chain to a root. The model notes the first arm is subsumed by base >= count either way, so the outcome is the same.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 an **addressed** row whose signed `for_key_id` is one of the period's two serve seats
side_b: CC 6.1.9 The door checks only that `for_key_id` names a serve seat, refusing otherwise (`census_return_recipient_not_seat`), never membership in the drawn pair.
note: Read as no conflict in the table. The registry row still describes the recipient as one of the drawn pair, while its own refusal list has only the not-a-seat refusal. CC 6.1.9 governs.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 0 or 1: which of the two additive shares, and which aggregator's partial. Any other value is census_share_index_invalid.
side_b: CC 3.1.3 `ballot_share_duplicate_token` and `ballot_share_pair_incomplete` as for the census share.
note: The member-share rows take ballot_* names for two refusals in CC 3.1.3 and census_* names for the index and the expiry (census_return_expired) in CC 2.6.1.7. Which token a member share with index 2, or one offered late, is refused by is not stated for the family.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 a cell with fewer than **k = 10** owners is merged upward and then withheld as *below the floor* (`census_composite_below_k`)
side_b: CC 6.1.9 The door refuses a composite with fewer than **k = 10** sources (`census_composite_below_k`).
note: One token names a door refusal of a whole row (CC 3.1.3: source_count < 10) and a cell withheld inside a published row. CC 2.6.1.7 says "the cell is refused". A reader resolves it as: aggregators merge small cells before publishing, the door refuses a row whose source_count is under ten.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 a first-run or consent item runs the self row, one voice of one, no window
side_b: data manifests/choice_item.cddl (self_choice for a first-run or consent item)
note: The text says the item's policy is "a row of the governance policy table above". The table has no self row with no window: its two self rows are the self-roster add and evict, 86 400 s, one voice a key. The CDDL names the policy self_choice and manifests/transitions.json names it selfAct; neither is a row of constitution/governance_policy.tsv. A validator that requires a table row refuses every first-run item.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 **Announcing starts on,** its cost on screen.
side_b: CC 5.4.6 So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding
note: To fix from the text, and not yet fixed: the default-on sentence of CC 4.5.13 still carries no exception for an owner with no age assurance on record, who reads as under 13. The same paragraph's rule "A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are" stands beside it.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 REQUIRED on consent:state:granted and on delegates_to
side_b: CC 3.3.1 A `granted` naming no scope matches nothing, by design.
note: Is a grant with no scope refused at the door or admitted as a grant of nothing? CC 2.1 says both in one row. CC 2.6.1.2 lists scope with the optional members ("absent", "member absent"), unlike its rows for required members, which read "on one, admission refuses". CC 3.3.5 admits a consent_record with stance granted on three required fields, scope not among them. The family model's body for consent:state has no required scope. The text leans to admitted and matching nothing; the signed-object table says required.

side_a: CC 3.3.1 Closed-set stance values; `revoked` overrides prior `granted`.
side_b: CC 3.1.5 `{stance}` ∈ `granted` \| `revoked` \| `expired` — closed; `expired` is the one substrate-emitted value.
note: The CC 3.3.1 row is headed `consent:state:{granted\|revoked}` and calls that set closed; CC 3.1.5, CC 3.3.5 and the registry (three values, open false) add expired, emitted by the substrate when valid_until passes. A door built from CC 3.3.1 refuses a peer substrate's consent:state:expired row as outside a closed vocabulary. The registry supports three.

side_a: CC 2.1 | `expires_at` | `membership:proposal`, REQUIRED |
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end
note: The signed-object table gives expires_at as OPTIONAL and names the families where it is required: the two census shares only. CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.2 require it on a membership proposal ("on one, admission refuses") and CC 3.1.3 on a lineage_witness proposal ("with a required `expires_at`"). The family model carries the membership requirement with presence "unstated". A door driven by the table admits an invitation that never expires.

side_a: CC 2.1 | `role` | `membership:proposal`, nullable; restated on `membership:acceptance` |
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 an explicit JSON null on any optional member is refused federation_malformed_row / envelope_member_null
note: Nullable in CC 2.1, "`null` (no role offered)" in CC 2.6.1.2 and "key_id | null", "null = indefinite" in the consent_record block of CC 3.3.5 read as a member written with JSON null. CC 2.6.1.7 says for oversight_mode that null means absent and that a written null is refused; it does not say so for role. A producer that writes "role": null has its proposal refused.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 the envelope members `axis`, `at_rest_sha256`, `owner_key_id`, `community_key_id`, `minter_key_id`, `epoch`, `stream_id`, `wrap_algorithm`, `wrapped_dek`
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1 recipient_key_id: new_member_key,
note: The fenced cascade of CC 4.4.3.4.1 writes a grant with recipient_key_id and content_sha256, members that CC 3.3.2 does not list (the recipient is attested_key_id, the blob is at_rest_sha256); the block's own comment says the recipient is attested_key_id. The family model and the CC 8.10 card for key_grant carry both sets as "text only". CC 3.3.2 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 a fourth reading is a separate member, which is why consent_supersedes exists
side_b: CC 3.1.2.1 The member cites a row on any attestation type, and takes composer meaning only on `supersedes` / `withdraws` / `recants`.
note: Held in the table. Registered families use references_attestation_id on scores rows (membership and lineage-witness answers, deferral responses, the build attestation), which CC 3.1.2.1 allows; CC 2.6.1.7 reads the member only by row type on the three composers, and CC 3.5 defines a standalone attestation as one with no `references_attestation_id`. Still as written.

side_a: CC 2.2 declares its `oversight_mode` and `witness_relation` per [CC 2.1](#2.1)
side_b: CC 2.1 | `witness_relation` | `external` |
note: The conformance class has a producer declare both members; CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 make both optional, absent reading as external and as the per-cell default. A producer that omits them is conformant under the tables and not under the class sentence read strictly. The tables govern admission.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7 The `{scale}` vocabulary above has seven tokens.
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json "open": true, "segment": "{scale}", "values": ["self"]
note: The registry, generated from the Part 3 table, holds one of the seven scale tokens (the row separates them with commas where other rows use bars) and marks the vocabulary open. The text lists seven and forbids adding federation; it does not call the set closed, so by CC 3.1.7 it is open, and the forbidden token is admitted by the registry.

side_a: CC 3.4.4 On the **removal** path the substrate emits the *same* `hard_case:family_membership_change:{family_key_id}`
side_b: CC 3.4.4 the scored dimension is `hard_case:{kind}` ([CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md)) and a substrate emits the kind
note: The section says the key-suffixed spelling is for readability and is never emitted, then says the substrate emits it. The first sentence and CC 3.1.9.4 govern: the dimension is hard_case:family_membership_change and the key is in the payload.

side_a: CC 3.3.5 3. topical_relation:bilateral_pair links the two Contributions
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.3 recommended, not required for ratification — `bilateral_pair_id` is the binding mechanism
note: The fenced pattern of CC 3.3.5 lists the edge as a step of the pair and writes each half as a consent_record plus a scores row; CC 4.4.3.5.3 makes the edge optional and CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 makes a half one scores row of subject_kind consent_record. The Part 4 statements are the later and the normative ones.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling.
note: Tolerate reads as optional. CC 3.1.7 and the dimension shapes of CC 3.4.11 itself require the segment on both age families, and the registry rows carry {version} as a segment. CC 3.1.7 governs. Found by the second reading too and not in the table. The MAY parenthetical of C343 in the same paragraph is gone.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "A field's definition MUST declare which kind it is; absent a declaration, set-semantics (sorted) is the default."
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl (CC 2.6.1.7) "? consent_basis: [* consent-basis],  ; OPTIONAL (capacity:*, observation:access_assumption:v1); default absent; array kind: sequence"
note: CC 2.1 defines consent_basis with no array kind, so the 2.6.1.1.1 default makes it a set (an unsorted or duplicated array is refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted); the 2.6.1.7 table and the CDDL make it a sequence kept as authored. The table applies the same default to differs_in in so many words, so one of the two is unstated: either CC 2.1 declares the sequence or the table reads set. The `paths` array inside each entry has no kind either.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`membership:proposal`, REQUIRED"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end (census_return_expired after it)."
note: expires_at: CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.2 require it on a membership proposal; the 2.6.1.7 row (and the CDDL) gives presence OPTIONAL and names only the census shares as REQUIRED. CC 3.1.3.2 supports CC 2.1.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`membership:proposal`, nullable; restated on `membership:acceptance`"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "an explicit JSON `null` on any optional envelope member is refused as malformed"
note: `role` is called nullable in CC 2.1 and its default is written `null` in CC 2.6.1.2; a null on the wire is refused envelope_member_null. 2.6.1.1.1 says a default written null means absent, and the 2.6.1.7 row says OPTIONAL, absent; 'nullable' is the stale word.

side_a: CC 2.6.2 "Every ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 datetime in this specification MUST be:"
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl (CC 2.6.1.7) "rfc3339 = tstr  ; a column rendered by the store; the signed twin inside the envelope is rfc3339-ms"
note: The columns beside the row (asserted_at, expires_at, scrub_timestamp, pqc_completed_at; valid_from and valid_until on a key record) are typed as an unconstrained string, while CC 2.6.2 binds every datetime to the millisecond Z form and cosigned_at beside the row is typed rfc3339-ms. Whether typed_diverges_from_envelope compares strings or instants is unstated. The vectors render every column in the millisecond form.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "(no `0x`, no separators, byte-length-exact; never base64 in canonical bytes)"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 "The member carries both halves raw, in the standard base64 of [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.1.1), and JCS sorts its keys:"
note: Rule 2 says public keys are lowercase hex and never base64 in canonical bytes; onion_hop_pubkeys, encryption_pubkeys and pubkey_ed25519_base64 / pubkey_ml_dsa_65_base64 (hashed into every recovery commitment, CC 3.2) are public keys in base64 inside signed bytes. The next sentence of rule 2 admits 'fields explicitly documented as base64', which is how a careful reader resolves it; CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 repeats 'pubkey byte fields are lowercase-hex' two paragraphs from a base64 public key.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "elements MUST be **lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)** before signing"
side_b: CC 3.4.7.1 "the set MUST be encoded as its members sorted ascending by Unicode code point, deduplicated, comma-joined with no whitespace"
note: Three orders are named for one rule: UTF-16 code units (2.6.1.1.1), Unicode code points (3.4.7.1) and UTF-8 bytes (CC 3.2 recovery commitments, CC 3.3.7 consent targets, CC 3.1.2.1 capability_declaration). Code-point and UTF-8 order agree with each other and differ from UTF-16 order above U+FFFF. Every set named today holds ASCII tokens, so no byte moves; an open-vocabulary set would fork.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 "**Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule)."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "elements MUST be **lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)** before signing"
note: CC 6.1.1 sorts raw leaf bytes and names the 2.6.1.1.1 rule as its source, which sorts JCS strings by UTF-16 code unit. For a member id outside the BMP the two orders differ. CC 6.1.2.1.2 ('raw leaf bytes') and CC 6.1.5.2 ('sorted over UTF-8 bytes') support the byte reading; the citation is the loose part.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.3 "A CEG-Conforming Substrate (CCS) MUST preserve the as-received envelope object bytes for relay"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1 "A relay that re-serializes from a parsed object at all MUST emit JCS"
note: Known, read as no conflict: 2.6.1.3 defines the contract as the as-received object (member set and values), and whitespace and member order are outside it. The word 'bytes' in the first sentence is still there.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "`link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard)."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "`link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame"
note: Known, resolution 'to fix from the text': NOT yet fixed, both sentences stand at head 87c1730. A per-link counter and a per-(link, stream) counter give different outer nonces on a link that carries two streams, so frames fail to open.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`"
note: Known, resolution 'to fix from the text': NOT yet fixed. The section still lays out the v1 trailer in full and names the v2 form (with source_ms) as the shipping one without its layout; a relay built to either refuses the other's chunks as av_chunk_trailer_invalid.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "32 bytes (caller-derived: sha256(stream_meta))"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "`stream_id` (32 bytes, which MUST equal `SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v2" ‖ room ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce)` with no length prefixes)"
note: The byte layout's comment derives stream_id from an undefined stream_meta; the binding rule in the same section fixes the derivation for a call stream and a receiver re-derives it. The MUST governs; the comment is loose, and no derivation is given for a stream that is not a call.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "the **outer** seal is the per-RNS-Link transit wrap (a relay sees the outer layer only, never plaintext"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "under the [CC 5.3.3.2.5](#5.3.3.2.5) outer seal (AES-256-GCM), itself inside the link's [CC 5.3.3.5](#5.3.3.5) E1 transit seal"
note: One sentence makes the outer seal the transit wrap itself (two layers, 'the E1 two-layer posture'); the other puts the outer seal inside a separate E1 transit seal (three layers); CC 5.4.2 says the chunk rides 'under the E1 seal'. The outer-nonce vectors pin the bytes, so a reader resolves it there, but the text names the layers two ways.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.5 "A blob cited only by a bare `evidence_refs[]` string has no declared size, and a consumer fetching it enforces the [CC 2.6.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md) cap instead."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 "the heavy payload moves to the blob plane as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to the holder count its owner chose"
note: The 2.6.1.3 cap is 1 MiB on an envelope's JCS bytes. Read onto a blob it refuses any bare-cited blob above 1 MiB, which is the very payload 2.6.1.3 sends to the blob plane and names 'by content hash in evidence_refs'. The two agree only if every above-cap payload is cited through a descriptor that carries its size (trace_manifest:v1 does); neither sentence says so.

side_a: CC 6.1.3 "the holding claim, the compress request and the capacity preimage — are **transport/substrate framing**: binary, never a CC 2.1 Contribution"
side_b: CC 2.1 "subscribers discover holders through the holding claims at the content's scope (`custody:ack:v1` `here` rows"
note: 'Holding claim' names two objects with two wire forms: the custody:ack:v1 row, a CC 2.1 row under JCS (Parts 2, 3, 5), and the chunk-level binary claim of CC 6.1.5 (Part 6). CC 6.1.5 calls the second 'the chunk-level companion of the whole-blob custody:ack:v1 report', which resolves it; CC 6.1.3's flat 'never a CC 2.1 Contribution' does not say which it means.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 "Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment."
side_b: CC 3.1.7 "A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling."
note: 'Tolerate' reads as optional; CC 3.1.7 requires the segment on every dimension but the two exempt families, and the next sentence of CC 3.4.11 gives both arities with {version}. The 3.1.7 rule governs; the 'tolerate' sentence is older wording.

side_a: CC 3.1.2 "Carries no version segment (`_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt`): the suffix is the hash."
side_b: CC 3.1.7 "Two families need none, and a tail on one is tolerated, never required"
note: Known and settled from the text: the matcher and the manifest admit an exempt family with or without a tail. The CC 3.1.2 row still reads as 'has none'.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 "The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`."
side_b: CC 3.3.2 "HPKE RFC 9180 base-mode shape; X25519 KEM + HKDF-SHA-256 KDF + AES-256-GCM AEAD. **v1**."
note: Known, held. 'v2 only' and CC 5.1 ('A DEK that is wrapped MUST be wrapped with wrap_algorithm: v2 ... never v1') against a closed-set table that still registers the v1 string and makes v2 mandatory 'for streaming epoch-DEK grants' only. A consumer MUST reject v1 only on a streaming epoch grant (CC 5.1), so a v1 wrap on a content grant is admitted by one reading and refused by the other.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on supersedes, withdraws, recants"

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "**Yes — self only, by possession**; every other row is admitted only once its signer's `key:record` is held (retryable otherwise)"

The 2.6.1.7 table lets the record's own scrub_key_id name an anchor, so the base signature is not the key's. A new record whose base scrub is an anchor's is admitted by the table's reader and refused by the other. The family model's note ('pre-rc8 anchor-scrubbed base admitted') suggests the table describes records already held; the CC 8.10 card says attest: self.

side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Serialised as roles; the record also carries roles inside the signed registration_envelope."
note: A key record carries its role set three ways: identity_type ('a set rendered as one string'), a roles array beside the record and roles inside the signed envelope. CC 3.4.7 says the gate reads identity_type and never a role inside the envelope; nothing says whether the roles array beside the record is the same set, or what holds when the two differ. CC 3.4.7.1 leaves the storage form to the implementer.

side_a: CC 2.6.8 "a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains"
side_b: CC 2.3.2.1 "A consumer verifies a `key_id`'s fingerprint suffix against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**"
note: Known and settled from the text as one act with its scope stated in CC 2.3.2.1. CC 2.6.8 still says 'resolving' and, in the next sentence, 'detected at registration and never at resolution'.

side_b: CC 3.3.14 "A bare `scores` Contribution on the registered dimension **`identity:canonical_binding:{canonical_hash}`**"
note: Known (proposed, not applied; for Eric). The row type of a canonical binding is delegates_to in CC 2.3.2.2 and scores in CC 3.3.14, and the two sections also differ on whether the binding opens rule 2. Still as it was.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "`evidence_refs[]` stays bare sha256."

'Bare' is said against a CID or multihash wrapper, and the field set and the signed-object vector (`sha256:9f86…`) carry the prefixed form; CC 5.3.2.5 says 'a bare URI or content-hash string'. A producer writing the unprefixed digest would fail the digest == evidence_refs[] comparison at a reader of the field set.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "codec           string         RFC 6381 family; REQUIRED for video/mp4, audio/mp4"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "**`format` and `codec` are required in clear iff `sealed_descriptor` is ABSENT.**"
note: The rule reads as requiring codec in clear on every unsealed struct, an image included; the field set and the codec bullet require it for video/mp4 and audio/mp4 only, and the seal carries it 'where applicable'. The field set is the narrower and the consistent one.

side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.2 "with an application-defined payload codec in place of an A/V codec"
note: CC 3.3.13 fixes a live_stream chunk as one fMP4 segment whose concatenation is a valid video/mp4. CC 5.3.3.2.1 and 5.3.3.2.2 make the realtime chunk payload opaque and application-defined (game ticks, CRDT operations, one chunk per ChunkLayer cell) on the same live_stream wire. A substrate cannot see inside a sealed chunk, so admission does not differ; what a recording of such a stream is, and whether it is attested as video, does.

note: The StreamKeyBinding of 5.3.3.2.3 is a closed fixed encoding (version, room, publisher, join_nonce, stream_id, epoch, chunk_key, two signatures) with no codec member and trailing bytes refused. The codec is a stream field of the CC 3.3.13 descriptor. 'The stream's binding' in 5.3.3.2.1 names something other than the binding the next section defines.

side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.1 "No scalable-coding semantics. `ChunkLayer` MUST be `{ 0, 0, 0 }`. Default for non-layered streams and for audio."
note: The opaque class 0xFF has one layer and carries audio; it has no floor tile to define, and 5.3.3.2.1 says 'an opaque stream is base'. 'Every codec_id class' should read every layered class.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane and never renders"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.6 "The ingest pipeline that makes Tier A enforceable belongs on the **node**, so every client renders only bytes the node's safe encoder produced."

They agree if 'node' in 5.3.2.6 is the opener's own node and its output is a rendition with derived_from; 5.3.2.6 says neither, and its table is marked recommended, not normative.

Still as it was.

side_a: CC 3.4.5: `consent:partnership_grant` MUST be emitted by a `subject_key_id` of the target Contribution or a `delegates_to` chain rooted at one

side_a: CC 3.3.7: Pinning `self` is what forecloses a third party forging a grant in G's name, since only G signs with G's key as the attested-intent-holder.

The family model (code-v61) and the CC 8.10 card admit both: `replication: owner, self`. A node built to CC 3.3.7 alone refuses the owner-signed grant that sets the per-node allow list.

side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: For a `family` member the admitting host runs the walk after the member is admitted.
note: The re-key walk wraps every blob the cohort holds, other members' blobs included, and "writes the grant rows"; CC 4.4.3.4.1 does not say whose key signs them. Under the sealer rule the admitting host speaks for its own owner only, so its grant over another member's blob is refused. reactions.json has the walk emit key_grant:content "by identity:substrate_persist".

side_b: CC 3.1.3: **Yes — addressed:** the returning node's key; reach is the named seat only
note: CC 6.1.9 makes eligibility depend on the node's owner-binding chaining to a bundle root; the census:share row lists the door's refusals and none is for an ineligible sender, and the model cell is `self`. Whether an unowned or unrooted node's share is refused or only uncounted is not said.

side_b: CC 4.3: An approval that authorises an identity amendment ([CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md)) is not handed on: it is signed by the conferrer or by the person holding the unscoped seat.
note: The deferral:response row lists three attesters with no exception; CC 4.3 (the home, cited by the row) withholds one class of approval from the agent. A door built from the row admits an agent-signed approval of an identity amendment.

note: CC 4.5.9.1 lets a holder of a `consent_revocation` delegation emit a location proof for the subject; CC 4.5.9.3 says only the subject's signature brings one into being, and CC 2.4.1.1 gives that scope to the rule-3 proxy for withdrawing only. Under the first a proxy (typically the agent holding the data) can state where a person is; under the second it cannot.

note: The emitter rule keys on membership alone; the composition paragraph adds a role-set condition and names no subscriber-eligible role. The model cell is `roster_member(at)` with no role condition, which follows the first.

note: Known, still there and marked for Eric: the enumeration of CC 4.2.1 lists lifecycle rows but not `accord:human_dignity`; the model gives every accord:* family the signer `seat_role(holder)`. C051 is the same enumeration against the CC 4.2.6 roster-change objects.

note: Known (to fix in the data) and still there: transitions.json gives takedown_notice:{basis} one attest transition, role `takedown`, policy selfAct, for every basis; no cosigned policy for the steward_purge leaf.

note: The text and the family model signer and cosign cells make transport:canonical_rebind a quorum act. manifests/transitions.json and the CC 8.10 card (which CC 8.10 calls this document's statement of the value) give its attest transition role `holder`, policy `selfAct`: one voice. Under the card a single accord holder re-binds a seated serve node's transport. Same fault as C307 for the steward_purge leaf.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2: Subject-scoped quarantine marker: **slash-duty-holder-only** emitter.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: {attester, subject} (+ producer's owner, consent proxy rule 3, delegate rule 4: outside vocabulary)
note: The quarantine:{state} lifecycle cell (code-v61), the transitions row and the CC 8.10 card let the subject of a quarantine marker withdraw it (`withdraw: author, subject`). The text gives the marker plane to the slash-duty holder alone and CC 2.4.1.1 "admits no subject-side removal of an adverse row"; quarantine is not among the families the `adverse` departure reason moves. The same default lets the subject withdraw a wa_adjudication finding and a mesh_config row. Belongs to the withdraw key as well.

side_a: CC 3.2: Ownership MUST be resolved by `owner_of`, which reads owner-bindings and nothing else
side_b: CC 3.4.7.3: The `identity_occurrence` half yields **at most one** anchor, and the custody half yields **at most one**
note: Known and held (ask persist), still there: CC 3.2 and the definition in CC 3.4.7.3 read the steward from the one live owner-binding and nothing else; the Cardinality paragraph of CC 3.4.7.3 keeps a second, occurrence anchor, under which an agent may act through a node of a person who holds no owner-binding on it. C209 (`steward_of ==` in the fenced line) goes with it.

side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: That signature is admissible only from a key with a live federation-scope owner-binding
note: Joining a public room needs an announced owner because the room's rows are served to strangers; founding one is said to carry no owner gate. A founder whose binding is held at self only is seated by the first and could not have joined by the second. The reason given for the joiner applies to the founder as well.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: require  attester(capacity) ∉ {S, petitioner}
side_b: CC 3.1.2: the subject cannot self-emit it and the proposed steward cannot be the attester
note: The predicate and the rejection list of CC 3.4.12 bar the steward and the petitioner as assessor; the CC 3.1.2 catalogue row and the registry reserved rule ("attester != steward") bar the steward only. Same shortfall as C012 found in the review list. The family model marks even the steward test as a gap.

side_b: CC 3.4.12: It is **rejected** when its `valid_until` outruns the review cadence
note: Two bounds on how long a substituted binding may run: the freshness window of the capacity attestation, and the review cadence (set by the community's policy and named in the row). The section does not say they are one period; where they differ the predicate enforces the cadence only.

side_a: CC 3.2: It is cosigned under that affiliation's protocol
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: affiliation named must admit the owner
note: For an agent held for an organisation the text requires the owner-binding to carry the affiliation's quorum; the ownership family's cosign cell is `none` (code-v61), its authorize transition is one voice (`selfAct`, role owner), and the placement cell reads the affiliation as only having to admit the owner. departure_reasons.json lists the cell as open. One steward's signature binds the organisation under the data and does not under the text.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: The substrate MUST refuse such a row whose `asserted_at` precedes the receiver's clock by more than `W`, with the refusal token **`asserted_at_stale`**.

note: Rule 1 and the lead of CC 4.5.4 read as "no moderator, no federation"; rule 2 and CC 4.5.13 keep the room readable and carry its ballots between nodes until one is seated, and only rule 3 stops it. A reader of rule 1 alone refuses the ballots the election needs.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: Members may read, and nobody may post, admit or act until a moderator is seated.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: **A steward, where one exists, MAY appoint a moderator directly at any point and end the vote.**
note: Nobody may act in a locked room, yet members sign ballots, withdrawals, an acceptance and a resignation, and a steward appoints. The lock is on posts, admissions and moderation; the sentence says more.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: Enoch-Arden return ↔ a new election on a lapsed steward's silence
side_b: CC 4.5.4: When a community has no live holder of `moderate`,
note: The symmetry line triggers an election on a steward's lapse; rule 2 of CC 4.5.4 and the election paragraph trigger it only when no holder of `moderate` is live. A steward who lapses beside a live moderator opens no election under the rule.

side_a: CC 4.5.4: The creator **names one at creation** (founder responsibility).
side_b: CC 4.5.13: At creation the creator chooses their own role: **steward + moderator**, or **moderator only**.
note: CC 4.5.4 lets the creator name any member as the first moderator; CC 4.5.13 makes the creator a moderator in either choice.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: Weight = Credits × expertise multiplier.
side_b: CC 1.13.2: One voice counts once
note: CC 3.1.9.6 calls credits "Non-transferable governance weight" and a `vote:{contribution_id}` is weighted by them; CC 1.13.2 and CC 4.5.13 count one vote per person in every governance act. Consistent only if this vote is a score on a Contribution and never a governance count, which the two rows do not say.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.1: That plane is steward-authored, time-limited, and able only to **relieve**
side_b: CC 4.2.1: The root's own quorum MAY establish a durable setting directly (cold)
note: CC 6.1.5.1 and CC 4.2.1.4 ("why both expire", "an expiring relief") make every mesh_config row time-limited; rule (3) of CC 4.2.1 bounds only the threshold-1 emergency form and lets a quorum set a durable one. reactions.json follows CC 4.2.1: expiry is required for the `emergency` leaf alone. A reader of CC 6.1.5.1 refuses a durable row.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.1: `shaping.rho`, `shaping.window_secs`, `shaping.node_cap_bytes_per_s` ([CC 5.4.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md))
side_b: CC 5.4.3: cover is a property of a link, not of a node
note: Settled in principle, no repair applied; the key is still in all three lists and CC 5.4.3 still defines no node-wide cap. Under rule (2) a key with no consumer is refused at admission.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.7: "if the member's local substrate chose to re-emit the community content at `cohort_scope: self` for cross-device sync; otherwise community content stays at the cohort_scope: community visibility on each device"
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3: "A node is set up as **personal** by default, and a personal node's allow list is all of its owner's cohorts."
note: Whether a member's other devices receive community content: CC 4.4.3.2.7 makes it depend on a local re-emit at self scope; CC 5.2 and CC 6.1.5.3 put every claimed node of a member in the audience, by pull anti-entropy and under the allow list, with no re-emit. The rest of the text supports side B.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "every `cohort_scope: self` Contribution's DEK wraps to both, so **the app and the agent decrypt the same Self content**"
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3: "With no `cohorts` member a personal node receives every cohort its owner is in and a server node receives no `self` or `family` content."
note: Does an agent occurrence, or a home server, receive its owner's self content. CC 6.1.5.3 puts `agent` and `server` in the server class, and CC 3.3.7 says `self` is never listed, so no grant can add it. CC 4.4.3.4.3, the CC 3.3.4 worked example (alice_agent_key, alice_homeserver_key) and CC 3.3.6 deliver self content to those occurrences. Nothing decides between them.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: "a federation-scoped `scores` row by the founder carrying the room's name, description, `cohort_subkind`, admission policy, named moderator and `community_key_id`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.8: "An affiliation that is not public carries a federation-scope listing row (`community:listing:v1`, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) naming those four things and nothing else."
note: What the public listing row is and holds. CC 3.1.1 and CC 3.2 make it a public community's row with name, description, admission policy and named moderator, and say a private community has no directory entry. CC 4.4.3.2.8 gives a non-public affiliation one, holding existence, key id, officers' roles and licence classes only. The family model body has name, description, cohort_subkind, community_key_id.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.1: "An observer learns that a group exists, roughly how big it is, and when its membership churns."
side_b: CC 5.2: "nothing of the content, of the roster or of who holds it"
note: What an outsider learns of a bounded group. C240 is proposed and not applied: the CC 1.13.3.1 wording stands unchanged (ids ride the envelope, membership changes emit hard_case rows into the log), while CC 5.2 and CC 2.4.1.1 keep roster rows inside the audience that already holds the roster.

side_a: CC 5.2: "all current identity_occurrences of C.attesting_key_id whose node's allow list names the cohort (CC 6.1.5.3)"
side_b: CC 3.3.7: "**`self` is never listed**: a node's `self` content follows its class default and the two arms below."
note: The CC 5.2 enforcement block (the repair for C291) tests a self recipient by "allow list names the cohort", but the list can never name self. Read alone it gives no self wrap to a personal node that carries any explicit list. CC 3.3.7 is the wire home and decides: class default. Related: C174, C291.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "reaches it by **pull anti-entropy** on the one replication carrier — never by push, and never waiting on a user's action"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.6: "For `delivery_mode: push`, the substrate fans out to `entitled ∧ reachable`"
note: CC 6.1.5.3 says every row and blob of a cohort arrives by pull and never by push; CC 4.4.3.2.6 and CC 5.3.3.4 define a push delivery mode for a community stream. A careful reader takes the live plane as the unstated exception. Near C315 and C335, which are about the relay tree.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.6: "consumer reads `community_id` envelope field, walks the membership, filters out non-member peers from the discovery surface"
side_b: CC 5.2: "The holding claims of `community` and `affiliations` content reach the roster's members only, in the same way."
note: Who keeps community holding claims from outsiders: the consumer by filtering what it sees (CC 4.4.3.2.6) or the sender by never serving them (CC 5.2, CC 3.1.3.3). The audience rule is the home; the filter is a second check at most.

side_a: CC 6.1.9: "held by the author's node and the recipient's node and by no other"
side_b: manifests/family_model.json census:share:{class} replication.audience: "targeted -> cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id); commons -> everyone"

side_b: manifests/family_model.json moderation:{allegation_type} replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: The model names an audience value existence_only and a two-part body for it, and no family carries it. A moderation record built from the data is served whole to the person named, so the reporter cannot be shielded as CC 4.5.5 allows.

side_a: CC 1.16.5: "Appointment, rotation, recusal, and appeals are external to this system’s control and follow explicit anti-capture rules."
side_b: CC 4.3: "A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else"
note: Who seats a Wise Authority. C290 says to fix from the text and it is not fixed: CC 1.16.5 still appoints under the Governance Charter, the lead of CC 4.3 restates it, and the CC 4.5.1 register row still has two thirds of the sitting board confirming members. side_a: CC 3.3.6: "admitted as an `identity_occurrence` of the user's `identity_key_id` is structurally speaking AS that identity"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "The agent's occurrence buys reading only. It signs no item of the person's queue"
note: Whether a row signed by an agent's occurrence key counts as the person's. C329 is repaired in CC 4.4.3.4.3 (the "two occurrences of one user identity" wording is gone), but CC 3.3.6 still says the agent speaks as the identity. CC 4.4.3.4.3, CC 4.5.13 and CC 1.15.11 support side B.

side_a: CC 4.3: "on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum"
side_b: CC 4.3: "re-routes under rule 1 to the party's other live seats and, with none, to the conferrer"
note: Where an unanswered deferral goes. Rule 1 and the CC 3.1.9.3 row say "the live quorum", a body the seat rule of the same section does not have; the Withdrawal bullet names the party's other live seats and then the conferrer. The second is the seat model's rule. Residue of the board model (C290).

side_b: CC 3.1.9.3: "On expiry of the WA's freshness window it re-routes to the live quorum."
note: Which window lapses an unanswered deferral: the quorum's stated window, the WA's own window, or W of CC 2.6.7 (which CC 4.3 uses only to judge a response's signed instant). No number is given and no row carries one.

side_b: manifests/reactions.json: no entry for deferral:request or deferral:response:{outcome}; the CC 8.10 card for deferral:request has no line for what follows in time
note: The text has a clock on a deferral and a reaction at its close (re-route). The reactions manifest of 83 entries has none for the family, so a kernel run from the data leaves a deferral open and the agent inactive.

side_a: CC 7.3.5: "The Wise Authority adjudicates only the federation's own deferrals and in-federation objections"
side_b: CC 7.5.5: "The logs are under privacy-preserving seal, released only with WA approval or under lawful order."
note: CC 7.3.5 limits the Wise Authority to deferrals and in-federation objections. CC 7.5.5 has it approve release of sealed logs, CC 7.5.3 lets a "WA injunction" open a sunset assessment, and CC 7.3.6 says "WA oversight upholds the duties of creation". Each can be read as a deferral answered, but none says so.

note: The Retirement Standard owes a signed preserve request for every retired artefact; the model holds preserve_request, preserve_response and retirement:{state} shut with the reason "unbuilt". The data is behind the text and says so.

note: Which licence row is current. CC 3.3.9: latest signed instant, tie on the smallest attestation id, and "the substrate's merge never counts signers". CC 5.3.2.3: quorum weight first, then time, then content hash, with the more restrictive state winning. Two nodes holding the same rows can read a licence as active and as suspended. Nothing decides.

side_b: CC 4.2.6: "rotates by a `supersedes` signed under the recovery key"

More cases of a supersedes by another signer than C333 lists: a key rotation (the new record is attested by the new key), the holders' transport:canonical_rebind over a node's own binding, a listing changed by a moderate-holder. The model cell reads same_attester and notes "the door admits any signer's supersedes".

side_b: CC 3.1.7: "so a consumer resolving its authority falls through to the producer-steward default"
note: Still open for the steward: refuse a row of an unregistered family, or admit it under the producer-steward default. Both sentences stand. CC 2.4 gives a third treatment for a row of an unregistered type already held: reported, not served, not replicated, not deleted.

side_a: CC 4.5.7 a [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5) `moderate`-scope holder **optionally** enables a watchlist (`watchlist:{id}`, [CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md)) for a group they moderate

note: One sentence lets only a moderate holder enable a watchlist; the next (and the CC 3.1.9.4 row: "signed by the CC 4.5.5 `moderate`/`takedown` authority") also lets a takedown-only holder. The separation-of-powers table in CC 4.5.7 says `moderate`-holder.

CC 8.10 says the card is the statement of the value. The text is the side the rest supports.

side_b: CC 4.5.3 The windows are `Dmca512` 10 days, `DsaArticle16` 14 days, `OsaIllegalContent` 14 days and `CommunityStandards` 30 days.
note: The CommunityStandards withhold window is the operator's to set in the CC 3.3.2 table and a fixed 30 days in CC 4.5.3; constants.tsv (withhold_window_community_standards) sides with CC 4.5.3. The window decides when held bytes are hard-deleted. Same family as C171 (Dmca512), which did not cover this row.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 Expeditious-with-counter-notice (OSA-defined timelines)
side_b: CC 4.5.3 `DsaArticle16` 14 days, `OsaIllegalContent` 14 days and `CommunityStandards` 30 days
note: CC 3.3.2 leaves the OSA window to the statute and gives DsaArticle16 no window at all; CC 4.5.3 and constants.tsv fix both at 14 days. CC 3.3.2 names the window only for Dmca512.

side_a: CC 4.5.3 The windows are `Dmca512` 10 days, `DsaArticle16` 14 days, `OsaIllegalContent` 14 days and `CommunityStandards` 30 days.
side_b: CC 8.10 card takedown_notice:{basis}: [Dmca512] clock `withhold` = `withhold_window_dmca512` (CC 4.5.3)
note: manifests/reactions.json and the card carry the stop-serving, withhold clock and destroy-at-close entries for Dmca512 only. DsaArticle16, OsaIllegalContent and CommunityStandards have constants (withhold_window_dsa16, _osa, _community_standards) and no reaction, so data alone neither withholds nor deletes under them. The immediate-removal reaction is also entered twice (cc_ref CC 6.1.2.2 and CC 4.5.13), once without the hard_case emit.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 Content survives **only** by an affirmative, on-record **keep-decision**
side_b: CC 4.5.13 When the live-majority vote **favors removal/moderation but the content is retained** (flagged, not hard-removed), it is **auto-hidden behind an active interstitial**.
note: The protective default gives two outcomes for a report raised in the room (removed unless a keep lands). The infohazard gate and the ladder give a third, "flagged-but-retained", when the majority favours removal, and nothing says when a vote for removal retains the bytes behind the interstitial and when it removes them. One reader destroys, the other keeps consent-gated.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A **report filed privately with the duty holder** (the named moderator, or the steward) opens no window and is seen by nobody but the duty holder.
side_b: CC 8.10 card moderation:{allegation_type}: [harm_report] on close(window) unless fold(keep_decided): read withdrawn (CC 4.5.13)
note: CC 4.5.5 says a harm report filed with the moderator is the `moderation:{allegation_type}` row under the moderate duty, and CC 4.5.13 says that report opens no window; the action raised in the room is "a report→`scores` Contribution". manifests/reactions.json hangs the 48 h default-removal clock on the moderation:harm_report leaf, the duty holder's record, and none on the room's scores proposal. Text side of this is C137; the data is not in the table.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 the proposal is tallied by **live-majority vote over the community's live members**
side_b: constitution/governance_policy.tsv, row moderation_action, floor cell: 1/2
note: The text asks a majority of those who show up ("A silent member is not in the denominator"; "a vote-to-keep that carries its majority"). The row gives floor 1/2, which the table defines as "at least the fraction", over base `active` (the standing roster up to 12): governance_policy_vectors.json lands it on 1 voice at base 2. Exactly half, counted over the roster, is not a majority of the present. The family model fold says over=present; the policy row says base active.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 `cancelled` for every community row, so a held change always resolves
side_b: constitution/governance_policy.tsv, row moderation_overturn, at_window cell: lapsed
note: The prose says every community row is cancelled at its window. Two rows of corridor `community` are not: `moderation_overturn` lapses and `moderator_election` stays open (governance_policy.tsv at_window). The rows agree with the prose about the lift and the election; the sentence about at_window is too wide.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 the count over exactly that set yields the signer, the set meets the floor, and the node's own 24 h since it first held the lock have passed
side_b: CC 8.10 card ballot:moderator: clock `window` = `moderator_election.window_secs` (CC 4.5.13)
note: The text runs the 24 h from the instant a node first held the lock, which no row carries ("Nothing signed opens an election"). manifests/reactions.json keys the clock on the family ballot:moderator from first_held, which is the first ballot a node holds. A node that held the lock ten hours before the first ballot closes at different instants under the two.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 a `moderation:{allegation_type}` ModerationEvent ([CC 3.1.9.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) adjudicated by quorum under the `moderate` delegated duty
side_b: CC 4.5.13 **This document imposes no quorum *on* a moderator or a steward; a community MAY impose one on itself (below).**
note: CC 3.4.11 has an age misdeclaration adjudicated by a quorum under the moderate duty. CC 4.5.13 and the card (moderation:{allegation_type} attest, selfAct, cosign none) have a moderator resolve by one signature unless the community chose a moderator quorum. One reader refuses a single-signed misdeclaration event; the other admits it.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2 `{allegation_type}` ∈ `rogue_vote` / `coordinated_voting` / `out_of_distribution_attestation` / `external_inducement_evidence` / `expertise_fraud`.
side_b: CC 3.4.11 It routes to the `moderation:age_assurance_misdeclaration` adjudication path
note: The registry row lists five allegation types with no "open" or "closed" word; CC 3.4.11, CC 3.4.12 (`moderation:capacity_misattestation`) and reactions.json (leaf harm_report) use three more. manifests/namespace_registry.json reads the segment as open vocabulary with the one value rogue_vote, dropping the other four listed. A reader who takes the list as closed refuses the other three.

A signer who left between signing and receipt counts under one and not the other, so the same event is admitted or refused. CC 2.6.7 and the membership model support the signed instant.

side_a: CC 4.2.6: **one holder's signed row** — pre-signable; no live set, no vote

note: CC 4.2.6 and CC 4.2.1.1 fire the halt on one holder's row with no live set and no count; the closing sentence of CC 4.4.3.4.2.1 still has the halt fire on the live set (so does the CC 3.2 T7 aside "with a live set and a floor-of-1 fire"). Stale wording; CC 4.2.6 is the home.

side_b: CC 3.3.4: served to the members who were active at the event's signed instant and are members still, and to no one else

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: A `licensure:{community_key_id}` row is a **cosigned row** ([CC 2.4](#2.4)) whose protocol source is the authority named in the dimension.
side_b: manifests/family_model.json: licensure:{authority_id} cosign_rule "none" (code-v61); transitions.json attest registered, policy selfAct; withdraw author, selfAct
note: The text makes an organisation-named licence a cosigned row under the affiliation's protocol (CC 3.3.9: a signature set short of it MUST NOT issue one), withdrawn only under rule 0. The data and the CC 8.10 card admit any registered single signer and let the author withdraw alone, with no branch for an organisation authority. The card is normative where it states a value, so the two cannot both be followed.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: the accord-holder family per [CC 4.2](part_4_composition_governance.md) decides by a strict majority of its standing roster
side_b: CC 5.3.4: It finishes at **M distinct holder authorizations** (the charter's `quorum:2/3`
note: The accord family's protocol is named `majority` (entrenched) in CC 3.3.4 and the charter's `quorum:2/3` in CC 5.3.4; under absolute M the two diverge once the roster grows, which CC 5.3.4 patches with max(M, strict majority). The CC 3.1.3 rebind row says only "the accord charter's threshold". C040 settled it for the standing-roster majority; the 2/3 wording is still in CC 5.3.4.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.6: For accountable streams, "published" means **witness-cosigned** (the CC 5.3.1 path), so the subscriber cannot collude with the producer on a private root.
side_b: CC 8.10: attest: `one transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}@admitted[val:log_id=leaf:stream_id,val:root_hash=val:chunk_root,leaf:tree_size>=val:K] else refuse` (CC 5.3.3.6)
note: The text asks a witness-cosigned root only of an accountable stream; a best-effort stream publishes a producer-signed root and its witness cosign is optional (CC 5.3.3.3). The delivery_receipt guard in transitions.json and its CC 8.10 card refuses every receipt with no admitted transparency_log:cosigned row, so a node built from the card refuses receipts on best-effort streams the text admits.

side_a: CC 2.4: transparency-log heads and cosigns ([CC 5.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) framing)
side_b: CC 3.1.2: Witness cosignature on an STH (substrate-conformance path; see [CC 5.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) endpoints). Witness-emitted, verify-recognized
note: CC 2.4 lists log heads and their cosigns as off the plane, not claims; CC 3.1.2 registers transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size} as a family of rows with a reserved emitter (CC 3.4.10), and the delivery_receipt guard reads such rows. A reader cannot tell whether a witness cosign is a framed object only, or also a row. CC 3.4.10 says the lineage-head cosign is "not an attestation row"; nothing says so for the STH cosign.

side_a: CC 3.1.2: emitter rule (`identity_type="witness"`) at CC 3.4.9
side_b: CC 3.4.10: `transparency_log:cosigned:*` is reserved: emitter rule is `attesting_key_id` MUST match a `federation_keys` row with `identity_type="witness"`
note: Citation: the CC 3.1.2 registry row and the CC 3.4.5 log-infrastructure bullet send the reader to CC 3.4.9 (co-stewarded prefixes) for the witness emitter rule; the rule is CC 3.4.10, which CC 3.2 T6 cites correctly.

side_a: CC 3.2: A cosignature on a head is verified against the directory of that head's **parent**, and the genesis head against the bundle's charter.
side_b: CC 5.3.1: against the witness's key record in the **charter's** witness directory for that lineage (never a directory of its own)
note: CC 3.2 T6 and CC 5.3.4 verify a lineage cosignature against the parent head's directory, never the head's own charter; the Registry route in CC 5.3.1 says only "the charter's" directory. On a head that changes the directory, a Registry reading CC 5.3.1 alone may count the new directory's witnesses. CC 3.2 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.6.5: Certificate Transparency v2.0 (CT-bis); MUST be used for new transparency-log integrations; older 6962 instances continue to interoperate
side_b: CC 5.3.3.3: `root_hash` is the [RFC 6962](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6962) Merkle root over the first `tree_size` leaves
note: CC 2.6.5 makes RFC 9162 mandatory for new log integrations; the stream log (CC 5.3.3.3, CC 5.3.3.7), the cosign request (CC 5.3.1.1) and the CC 3.1.2 rows name RFC 6962. CC 2.6.1.8 notes the tree hashing is the same, so roots agree; the proof and structure formats named differ.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: An `identity_occurrence` row is signed by a live roster key of the identity (the genesis key or any admitted occurrence) and lands under the two-path policy
side_b: CC 4.5.12.3: A new `identity_occurrence` is admitted on a signature from EITHER the root `identity_key_id` (until the self evicts its genesis key) OR any currently active occurrence of that identity
note: CC 3.3.6 lands every occurrence admission by the two paths (majority at once, or the lone path after 86 400 s); CC 4.5.12.3 is headed single-vouch, admits on one signature, and its rationale rejects multi-vouch, then sends a user-role key to the roster door. Read whole, 4.5.12.3 splits by role; CC 3.3.6 states no split. CC 3.3.6.3 and the self_roster policy rows are the home.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: Lapse of a grant when `valid_until` passes without renewal.
side_b: CC 3.3.1: which it emits for a lapsed grant (`expires_at`, or a `retain:<window>` in the scope) with `consent_supersedes` naming the grant
note: Two cells of one table name different members whose passing lapses a grant: valid_until (also CC 3.3.5, CC 4.4.3.5.5, reactions.json) against the row's expires_at or a retain window in the scope. CC 2.1 holds valid_until and expires_at independent. A grant carrying only one of them lapses under one reading and not the other. The read path also names the link `supersedes_id` where this cell says `consent_supersedes`.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: A **confirmed** halt carries no TTL: expiry would convert the brake into a wait-out for the halted party
side_b: CC 8.10: expiry required `valid_until` max `accord_heartbeat_max_secs` (CC 3.4.1)
note: reactions.json and the CC 8.10 card put the heartbeat's required valid_until (at most 90 days, then read stale) on accord:lifecycle:{kind}, the confirmed and active rows. CC 3.4.1 gives that cadence to the heartbeat accord:lifecycle:v1, "a different row", and CC 4.2.1.3 gives a confirmed halt no TTL. A node built from the card ages a confirmed halt out; the heartbeat family accord:lifecycle has no expiry entry.

side_a: CC 3.2: The ≤ 90-day refresh cadence of `accord:lifecycle:active` is not a validity leg either
side_b: CC 3.4.1: `accord:lifecycle:active` is the resumption kind, a different row
note: CC 3.2 T4 gives the 90-day refresh cadence to accord:lifecycle:active; CC 3.4.1 and CC 3.1.1 give it to the heartbeat accord:lifecycle:v1 and make active the resumption after a halt. The T4 wording is the stale name and is the likely source of the misplaced expiry entry in reactions.json.

side_a: CC 4.2.6: within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1: The fuse is counted from receipt on the node's own clock, never from the signer-chosen `asserted_at`.
note: The CC 4.2.6 table measures the confirmation "of the halt" with no instant named; CC 4.2.1.1 runs the fuse from each node's own receipt. C039 settled it for per-node receipt and reactions.json follows (from first_held, by receipt); the table wording is unchanged.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: `delegation_valid_until` is **REQUIRED, at most 365 days (365 × 86 400 s) after `delegation_valid_from`**
side_b: CC 3.4.12: delegates_to.valid_until <= T2_review_cadence
note: The envelope member of a delegates_to edge is delegation_valid_until (CC 2.4.1, CC 2.6.1.7); the CC 3.4.12 predicate requires `delegates_to.valid_until`, and valid_until is a different member with a consumer-staleness meaning (CC 2.1).
